title: The reduced Principal carries the roles the provider record declares, and the union is refused on a malformed claim
asA: operator signing in through an OAuth2 provider whose token exchange returns roles at a project-declared claim path
iWant: the session-bridge to read the roles the provider record names and put them on `request.auth.roles`
soThat: project routes gate on roles without reading raw provider claims

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the provider record declares `roleSources: ["realm_access.roles"]` and the verified id_token carries `realm_access.roles = ["admin","auditor"]`, the reduced Principal's `roles` array is the set `{"admin","auditor"}`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a provider record with `roleSources: ["realm_access.roles"]` and a verified id_token whose `realm_access.roles` is `["admin","auditor","admin"]`
acceptanceCriteria.then: `request.auth.roles` is a two-element array whose set membership is `{"admin","auditor"}`; the array ordering is not asserted but the set is; the audit sink records one `oauth2.roles_mapped` event carrying the count `2` and no role values

acceptanceCriteria.description: When `roleSources` names multiple paths, the reduced `roles` is the union.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a provider record with `roleSources: ["realm_access.roles","resource_access.web.roles"]` and a verified id_token whose `realm_access.roles = ["a"]` and `resource_access.web.roles = ["b","a"]`
acceptanceCriteria.then: `request.auth.roles` has set membership `{"a","b"}`; each string appears exactly once

acceptanceCriteria.description: A `roleSources` path resolving to a value that is not a string and not an array of strings refuses the session issue with `OAUTH2_ROLES_MALFORMED`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a provider record with `roleSources: ["realm_access.roles"]` and a verified id_token whose `realm_access.roles` is the JSON object `{"admin": true}`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the bridge throws `OAUTH2_ROLES_MALFORMED` naming the provider id and the offending path; no session cookie is issued; the audit sink records one `oauth2.roles_refused` event carrying the reason class and no claim values

acceptanceCriteria.description: A provider record with an empty or absent `roleSources` produces a Principal with an empty `roles` array; no error.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a provider record whose `roleSources` field is `[]` (or absent) and a verified id_token that carries a `realm_access.roles` field the provider does not name
acceptanceCriteria.then: `request.auth.roles` is `[]`; the session cookie is issued normally; no `oauth2.roles_refused` event fires

acceptanceCriteria.description: An `enrichPrincipal` hook, when configured, receives the Principal after `roles[]` is populated and its return value replaces the Principal on `request.auth`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a provider record with `roleSources: ["realm_access.roles"]` and a project-authored `enrichPrincipal(p) => ({ ...p, roles: [...p.roles, "audit-viewer"] })` hook
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session-bridge reduces the identity of a caller whose `realm_access.roles` is `["admin"]`
acceptanceCriteria.then: `request.auth.roles` has set membership `{"admin","audit-viewer"}`; the hook is invoked exactly once per session issue

acceptanceCriteria.description: Project routes never observe a raw provider claim; every role decision reads the reduced Principal.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the applied blueprint at v1.3.0 and a source-tree scan of the project's contributed routes
acceptanceCriteria.when: a static scan looks for reads of `id_token`, `userinfo`, or raw provider-claim shape from any project route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the scan reports zero raw-claim reads outside the flow-controller and session-bridge modules; every route's role-check reads `request.auth.roles`
